newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia king returns as tension ease in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king returns as tension ease in northwest.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk returned home from overseas medical treatment on Monday as the threat of violent clashes in a northwest city between two coalition government parties ebbed.
The king, who suffers from arteriosclerosis and other ailments, arrived to a low-key welcome from officials and diplomats led by parliament chief Chea Sim.

Co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and Hun Sen of the ex-communist Cambodian People's Party were not at the airport as the king flew in from China. Ranariddh is believed to be in Thailand.
The 74-year-old king is seen as a mediating influence in the relations between the two main parties in the coalition formed after U.N.-run polls in 1993 to avoid a return to war.

Sihanouk has taken pains to promote a neutral image and, in an apparent bid to dispel suspicions and calm tempers, pledged before his November 10 departure for China he would not get involved in politics nor support any political party.

Tensions between Ranariddh and Hun Sen and their parties have resurfaced in recent weeks, reflecting differences over mass defections from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement since August and a long-simmering dispute over power-sharing.

Tempers rose earlier this month after men calling themselves Khmer Rouge urban operatives defected to Hun Sen and claimed the opposition Khmer Nation Party was a Khmer Rouge front and that FUNCINPEC had tried to cover up this fact.
Days later, Hun Sen's brother-in-law was shot dead and the premier said his death was linked to these defections.

Boiling point was neared at the weekend, when a senior FUNCINPEC official ordered 5,000 soldiers on alert and threatened to use force to combat alleged CPP harassment in the northwest province of Battambang.
Serey Kosal, deputy governor of Battambang, acted after an altercation between CPP military police and FUNCINPEC soldiers on Friday that left one person injured in Battambang city.
But the two sides agreed at meetings on Sunday to withdraw their forces from Battambang, an aide to Serey Kosal said.
"We agreed to withdraw troops of both sides and to calm the situation so everything can be solved," Thlang Chansovanarith told Reuters on Monday.
Serey Kosal, who has long feuded with Battambang Governor Um Samy of the CPP, had written to seek the support of Ranariddh and Hun Sen to counter alleged CPP intimidation and harassment.
"The top levels of government must discuss the situation -- the prime ministers, the military commanders. Our forces here are full of anger," Serey Kosal told Reuters.
Analysts predicted differences would resurface ahead of elections in 1997 and 1998.
